title: Storm-triggered outage leaves parts of Clovis and Sanger without power, disrupts businesses
text:
Storm-triggered outage leaves parts of Clovis and Sanger without power, disrupts businesses - ABC30 Fresno

 Storm-triggered outage leaves parts of Clovis and Sanger without power, disrupts businesses 
 Power has been restored for thousands of customers in Clovis after over 7,000 were out on Wednesday. By Jason Oliveira Thursday, October 22, 2026 12:45AM Share CLOVIS, Calif. (KFSN) -- Parts of Clovis and Sanger were left without power during the season's first major storm after lightning struck a transformer, disrupting businesses, affecting traffic signals and prompting safety reminders from local officials and utility crews.
 Among the businesses impacted was a Deli Delicious at Shaw and Armstrong, which was forced to shut down shortly before the lunch rush.
 "It always hurts business when the power's out, of course we can't make any sandwiches and today was our first day for our new soups. So we were looking forward to a lot of sales...but," said Silas Sears, assistant general manager of the deli.
 PG &E crews worked through the storm to restore electricity to thousands of homes and businesses in Clovis and Sanger.
 "Just want to remind customers to be prepared, this is certainly not going to be the worst we see this winter storm season. Its a good reminder to get ready as we see the first of this weather coming through," PG &E spokesperson Jeff Smith said.
 The outage also affected several intersections in eastern Clovis, including Armstrong and Barstow. Emergency crews reported a minor injury to one driver at that intersection.
 "Biggest message right now, early storms and slick roads. Slow down, take your time going from point A to point B, be courteous," said Rob Rush of Clovis Public Utilities.

 After damaged lines were repaired and power was restored, activity increased at the Clovis Corporation Yard on Sunnyside Avenue as residents visited the city's 24/7 self-service station to pick up sandbags for protection against rising rainwater.
 "We encourage people to get sandbags, if they know they have an issue at their house get your sandbags early. When things really start coming down and we get some heavy rain we'll have such a demand that they'll be delays here at the yard to get those sandbags," Rush said.
 Officials also reminded residents to ensure PG &E has their current contact information as stormy weather continues.
